results.perfect: No false alarms and nothing missed. You told the real attack apart from the odd-looking but normal activity.

computer.title: COMPUTER VIEW > DEVICES ON THE NETWORK

events.title: Sign-in: cpatel
events.detail:
Account: cpatel (Carla Patel)
Where: Philippines
Device: WS-CARLA (registered)
Time: 02:34

Is this normal for this account? Look at who it is and what device she used.
events.explain: Carla works the night handover on her own registered laptop. A late hour alone is not an attack.

events.title: 9 failed sign-ins: anreyes
events.detail:
Account: anreyes (Anna Reyes)
From address: 185.220.101.47
Result: 9 FAILED sign-ins in a row
Time: 02:38

Nobody mistypes a password 9 times in a row. Look at where the tries come from.
events.explain: Many wrong passwords in a row from one outside address means someone is guessing the password.

events.title: Sign-in from Germany: anreyes
events.detail:
Account: anreyes (Anna Reyes)
Where: Germany
Device: UNKNOWN-7F3A (not registered)
Time: 02:43

Anna always signs in from the office, on her own laptop.
events.explain: A sign-in from another country on an unknown device, right after the failed tries, means the password guess worked.

events.title: Sign-in: bnguyen
events.detail:
Account: bnguyen (Ben Nguyen)
Where: Philippines
Device: WS-BEN (registered)
Time: 02:50

Ben is working late from home.
events.explain: Ben is a known user on his own registered laptop. It looks odd at this hour, but nothing about it is wrong.

events.title: BACKUP-01 to FS-01
events.detail:
From: BACKUP-01
To: FS-01
Data: 4 MB
Time: 02:35

Nightly backup sync between two company servers.
events.explain: Two company servers syncing a backup at night is routine.

events.title: Outside VPN session
events.detail:
From: 185.220.101.47 (outside the company)
To: VPN-GW
Type: inbound VPN session
Time: 02:43

This is the same address that tried Anna's password earlier.
events.explain: A VPN session from the same outside address that guessed the password. This is how the attacker got inside.

events.title: FS-01 sending data out
events.detail:
From: FS-01 (file server)
To: 185.220.101.47 (outside the company)
Data: 3.2 MB leaving the network
Time: 02:52

The file server rarely sends anything outside.
events.explain: A file server sending data to an outside address at night is data leaving the network. The attacker is taking files.

events.title: WS-BEN downloads an update
events.detail:
From: WS-BEN
To: update.example.com
Data: 12 MB
Time: 02:58

A laptop downloading a system update.
events.explain: A registered laptop fetching a system update from the vendor's update site is normal.

events.title: WS-CARLA
events.detail:
Device: WS-CARLA
Owner: Carla Patel
Event: screen locked
Time: 02:32

Registered device, normal activity.
events.explain: A registered laptop locking its screen is normal.

events.title: UNKNOWN-7F3A joined
events.detail:
Device: UNKNOWN-7F3A
Owner: none registered
Event: joined the network
Time: 02:44

Every company device is on the asset list. This one is not.
events.explain: A device with no registered owner joined the network. Real company devices are always on the list.

events.title: WS-BEN restarted
events.detail:
Device: WS-BEN
Owner: Ben Nguyen
Event: installed a software update and restarted
Time: 02:47

Registered device.
events.explain: Installing an update and restarting is normal maintenance on a registered laptop. Odd-looking is not always an attack.

events.title: PRN-FL2 restarted
events.detail:
Device: PRN-FL2
Type: floor 2 printer
Event: restarted
Time: 02:55
events.explain: Printers restart on their own from time to time. This is normal.

events.title: BACKUP-01 backup job
events.detail:
Server: BACKUP-01
Event: nightly backup job started
Time: 02:30

Scheduled job, runs every night.
events.explain: A scheduled nightly backup is routine.

events.title: DC-01: 17 failed sign-ins
events.detail:
Server: DC-01 (handles every login)
Account: anreyes
Event: 17 failed sign-ins in 11 minutes
Time: 02:41

Normal is 0 to 1 failed sign-ins.
events.explain: Many failed sign-ins in a row can mean someone is guessing passwords.

events.title: DC-01: password changed
events.detail:
Server: DC-01
Account: anreyes
Event: password changed
Time: 02:44

This came one minute after the sign-in from Germany.
events.explain: The password was changed right after the attacker got in. This locks Anna out of her own account.

events.title: FS-01: payroll.xlsx downloaded
events.detail:
Server: FS-01 (file server)
File: payroll.xlsx
Event: downloaded by anreyes
Time: 02:52

The account is the one that signed in from Germany.
events.explain: Payroll holds private data. Downloading it at 2 AM with a stolen account is the attacker's goal.

events.title: MAIL-01 mail sync
events.detail:
Server: MAIL-01
Event: mail sync completed
Time: 02:57

Routine background job.
events.explain: A mail server finishing its regular sync is normal.
